$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file.
tranche: T5 — identity/tenancy REST, the BFF transport, and the webapp cutover
purpose: T5's first act is a repair, and the repair is the reason the tranche can be
measured at all. `tenancy-prisma-only` is the containment rule whose own
comment says the wrapper package is banned because it 'is the exact door the
legacy tree walks through today' — meaning `apps/webapp`. It could not see
that door.
WHY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Every alternative in the rule's `to`
pattern was anchored on `node_modules/`. `@platos/tenancy-database` is a pnpm
WORKSPACE package, so a module resolver reports the workspace path. Node's
own resolver, run from apps/webapp/app/services/, answers:
@platos/tenancy-database  ->  internal-packages/tenancy-database/dist/index.js
There is no `node_modules/` segment anywhere in that path. That is the
resolution model dependency-cruiser uses through enhanced-resolve, and
`.dependency-cruiser.js` is generated FROM this rule — so the enforcer the
rule is compiled for was the one guaranteed to miss the tree the rule names.
THE HALF THAT DID WORK, STATED SO THE FIX IS NOT OVERSOLD.
`scripts/arch/arch-boundaries.mjs` resolves a bare specifier to
`node_modules/<specifier>` rather than to a file, so under THAT enforcer the
old pattern did match — and was still inert, because `DEFAULT_SCAN_ROOTS`
excludes `apps/webapp` during the strangler window. Measured on the base
commit: `arch-boundaries.mjs --scan-root apps/webapp/app` reports 9
violations, all `tenancy-prisma-only`, and `webapp-no-prisma` — whose `to`
pattern DOES carry the workspace path — reports 0, because it cannot see the
specifier form. Each rule was blind to the half of the shape the other could
see. The fix gives `tenancy-prisma-only` both spellings; widening the scan
root is the cutover's to land, and is NOT claimed here.
NOTHING IN THIS LEDGER NEEDS A DATABASE, A CONTAINER OR A DOCKER DAEMON.
Every entry is a file edit plus one `node --test` process.
T5's SECOND act is the BFF/canonical-store refusal, and it found a hole no gate
in this repository could see.
THE BRIEF SAYS: "The BFF may set secure cookies and perform redirects; it may
NOT query canonical stores. Prove that boundary with a refusal." The IMPORT half
of that boundary was already enforced — composition-root C1 permits exactly one
file in the tree to name an adapter package, which is stricter than rule (j) and
does bind a transport. The REACH half was not enforced at all.
`AppModule` publishes `adapters: SuppliedAdapters`, every transport is handed the
whole `AppModule`, and `PostgresTenancyAdapter` extends `TenancyRepository`. So a
BFF transport can write
app.adapters["postgres-tenancy"].findOrganizationBySlug(slug)
and read the canonical store with NO IMPORT AT ALL. That file was written, placed
under apps/core-api/src/transports/bff/, and TYPECHECKED against the real project
graph. Then every gate was run against it:
audit:arch-boundaries    PASS — blind to it
audit:composition-root   PASS — blind to it
audit:max-file-lines     PASS — blind to it
audit:sole-writer        PASS — blind to it
audit:env-access         FAIL — on its FILE-COUNT pin only, not the reach
C8 is the refusal. It is expressed as the PROPERTY rather than as a list of which
adapters happen to be stores, because a list goes stale the day a directory is
added: a transport reads the system through `contexts`, and `adapters` is the
composition root's working material. `app.module.ts` had already made this exact
argument in prose for the ONE port it lifts out — "reaching for
`adapters['redis-cache'].requests` would put an adapter's NAME in a transport" —
and nothing enforced it.
WHAT THIS TRANCHE DID NOT BUILD, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED IT.
The identity/tenancy REST surface is NOT in this branch, and the reason is not
budget. `apps/core-api` cannot authenticate an operator, so every route on that
surface would have had to take a `userId` from the request — an unauthenticated
cross-tenant read of every organization in the install.
`identity-access` is the only context that can say who a caller is, and it is not
composable. `composition/context-ports.ts` declines it and `installation.test.ts`
already checks the reason against the binding table rather than asserting it:
`RateLimiter` is bound to `redis-ratelimit`, which is on `UNIMPLEMENTED_ADAPTERS`
(its `src/adapter.ts` is an 8-line generated interface), and `SecretHasher`,
`TokenMinter`, `TotpCodeVerifier` and `MfaSecretCipher` appear on NO row of
`ADAPTER_BINDINGS` at all. Searched independently for this tranche: the only
implementations of those four in the entire tree are in
`packages/contexts/identity-access/application/testing.ts` — the context's own
in-memory doubles. Composing production identity from those is the failure mode
this programme has already named: "Test doubles lie: the contexts' own fakes mint
values PostgreSQL refuses, and every use-case suite passes with them."
So the surface is blocked on adapters that are WIN-251/WIN-258's to write, not on
anything T5 could have done. Building the routes anyway would have produced the
dead surface WIN-297 declined to create, with a cross-tenant hole in it.
T5's THIRD act is the cutover METER, and it exists because the denominator of
the acceptance clause could grow between two green CI runs.
Nothing in this repository counts the webapp's canonical-store call sites.
`arch-boundaries.mjs` is the enforcer that would and its `DEFAULT_SCAN_ROOTS`
excludes `apps/webapp` during the strangler window; `.dependency-cruiser.js` is
a generated artifact and dependency-cruiser is not a dependency of this
workspace, so nothing executes it. A cutover whose denominator moves while you
are cutting over is a cutover that does not finish.
THE FIGURE REPRODUCES A THIRD TIME, AND IT CAUGHT THIS GATE'S OWN FIRST DRAFT.
The brief states 15 operations in 11 files, reproduced twice. An independent
AST parse joined to ADR M0.3 §5.2's ownership map first reported 14 in 10 — and
the missing one was `app/services/auth.server.ts:75`, which imports the client
as `./database.server` while the ten route files use the `~/` alias. The draft
matched the alias STRING. That is precisely the failure this tranche's first
commit repaired in `tenancy-prisma-only`: a pattern written against one
spelling of an import, blind to the other. The gate now resolves specifiers to
FILES and reports 15 in 11.
AND THE ATTRIBUTION IS THE NEW INFORMATION. The 15 split as tenancy 10,
identity-access 2, secrets 2, and one `$transaction` that owns no row. So FOUR
of the fifteen belong to contexts the composition root cannot build at all —
which is what makes the cutover a multi-tranche job rather than a long one.
procedure: PROVE GREEN FIRST. The unmutated tree ran green before and after every entry
generated config matches the rules module. An entry whose suite was already
red proves nothing, and a 'kill' with no named failing line is VACUOUS.
EVERY ENTRY BELOW WAS APPLIED, RUN, AND REVERTED. The `kills` array quotes
the case names the runner actually printed as failing, and `killCount` is the
number of cases that went from pass to fail. An entry that could not be made
to fail is in `declared`, with the measured reason it could not — never
omitted, and never counted as a kill.

declared.name: M04 a new webapp file imports the banned specifier
declared.attempted: Four shapes were added to apps/webapp/app/root.tsx, one at a time: `export * from`, a bare `import "..."`, `await import(...)` and `require(...)`.
declared.result: NOT KILLED, and not a gap. The checker saw all four (measured: `arch-boundaries.mjs --scan-root apps/webapp/app` named root.tsx in every case), so the ACCEPTANCE case's two sides both grew by one file and continued to agree — which is the case doing its job, not failing to.
declared.why-unfalsifiable: The ACCEPTANCE case is a BIJECTION between the checker's findings and a byte scan of the tree, deliberately rather than a pinned count. A pinned count would have to be edited by every commit of the cutover, and an assertion a branch edits to stay green is the assertion shape this project has already paid for once (contract-map.mjs's `count: 18`). The property that a new importer must be VISIBLE is what M05 falsifies, from the other side.
declared.measured: 9 violations on the base commit and 9 on this branch — the same nine files, named individually rather than counted.

declared.name: the dependency-cruiser enforcer's own behaviour on the repaired pattern
declared.attempted: Running dependency-cruiser over apps/webapp with the regenerated .dependency-cruiser.js.
declared.result: NOT RUN. dependency-cruiser is not a dependency of this workspace — `.dependency-cruiser.js` is a GENERATED artifact whose only gate is `gen-dependency-cruiser.mjs --check`, which compares it to the rules module and never executes it. Adding the tool is a lockfile change this tranche did not take.
declared.why-unfalsifiable: The claim under test is about a resolver's answer, not about that tool's reporting. It is measured directly instead: Node's own resolver — the same model dependency-cruiser uses through enhanced-resolve — is called from apps/webapp/app/services/ in the CORROBORATION case, and the path it returns is the path the pattern is asserted against. The case names its skip reason when no install is present rather than passing silently.

declared.name: C8 catching a reach through a variable that is not obviously the composed application
declared.attempted: `const m = app; m.adapters['postgres-tenancy']` and `function f(x: { adapters: SuppliedAdapters }) { return x.adapters; }` — the reach laundered through an alias or a structural parameter type.
declared.result: CAUGHT, but for a reason that is weaker than it looks and is therefore declared rather than counted. C8 refuses ANY `.adapters` property read inside `apps/core-api/src/transports/**`, whatever the receiver is named, so an alias changes nothing. What it does NOT do is prove the receiver is the composed application.
declared.why-unfalsifiable: A transport that defined its own unrelated object with an `adapters` property would be refused too — a false positive this rule accepts on purpose. Establishing that a receiver IS the `AppModule` needs the type checker rather than the parser, and a type-directed gate is a different instrument with a different cost. The false positive is cheap (rename the property) and the false NEGATIVE it trades away is not (a canonical-store read no gate can see), which is the direction a containment rule should err in. Stated here rather than left for a reader to discover when the rule fires on something innocent.
declared.measured: 5 reach spellings caught, 1 prose-only file correctly ignored, live tree at 0 violations across 1580 files.
